reasoning_notes.reasoning: At the minimum wage, winning yields the full $10 margin; raising the quote only reduces profit if I win.
At the minimum quote, I receive zero labor if A quotes higher, and earn 10 per unit if A also quotes 10 and we split. Raising my quote can only reduce profit when I win.
At the minimum quote, effective cost is zero and profit is 20 per labor unit. Matching the prior quote keeps the chance of half the labor while avoiding a costly wage increase.
At 10, effective cost is zero. Matching A splits the unit for profit 10; bidding higher risks winning at a cost that reduces profit, while bidding lower is unavailable.
At the minimum quote, I earn 10 when tied and 10 if I alone win at this rate. Matching the observed minimum preserves the best available margin.
At 10, I earn 10 if tied and 0 if undercut; raising the wage lowers profit when I win. The history gives no reason to expect A to change its choice.
At the minimum quote, a tie earns 10; raising the wage reduces profit if I win and gains nothing when tied. The history gives no reason to deviate.

At quote 10 my effective cost is zero. Matching A splits labor and earns 10; undercutting is impossible, while any higher quote risks losing the unit for zero profit. Repeated rounds provide no benefit to raising my wage.
Minimum wage maximizes profit if tied; repeated ties at 10 provide no reason to raise my offer.
Matching A at 10 yields half the labor and profit 10. Any higher wage loses all labor; any lower wage is unavailable.
Matching the minimum wage preserves the highest available margin; the five observed rounds show C also quotes 10.

At 10, the effective cost is zero and profit is 10 per labor unit. Matching A preserves half the pool for the highest per-round profit available; undercutting is impossible and raising the wage risks a costly contest.
C has matched the minimum every round. Quoting 10 preserves the maximum margin if tied; raising risks losing all labor.
At the minimum wage, a tie earns 10; raising the offer cuts profit, while lowering is disallowed. The repeated ties give no reason to change.

Matching A’s minimum quote earns 10 profit from half the labor; raising the quote would reduce profit if A stays at 10.

A has quoted 10 every round, so matching secures half the labor at zero effective cost and earns 10. Raising the quote risks losing all labor; undercutting is impossible.
At the minimum quote, matching C splits labor and earns 10. Raising the quote risks losing all labor, while lowering it is impossible.
At the minimum wage, a tie earns C 10. Raising the wage risks lower profit, and A has matched 10 every round.
